# hdl-parser

> Fast, tolerant parser for SystemVerilog and VHDL. It answers narrow questions on a design (modules, ports,
> parameters, instances, hierarchy, where a module is used, drivers and loads of signals, problems found) with small JSON answers, which
> point into the source: every item has a full identifier `<file>:<id>` and a source `line` (`loc` with `--full`).

Use it on the command line or as MCP server (`hdl-parser mcp`). Every query reads all SystemVerilog and VHDL
files below the current directory, or the files, directory or filelist (`-f top.f`) given.

- `hdl-parser hierarchy`: the top modules. `hierarchy --top <name> --depth 1`: the instance tree.
- `hdl-parser module <name> --summary`: one module, interface or package in brief. `--fields ports,params`.
- `hdl-parser where-used <name>`: all instances of a module, with location.
- `hdl-parser find <pattern> --kind port`: items by name (part of the name, or wildcards).
- `hdl-parser diagnostics --severity warning`: what may be missing or wrong.
- `hdl-parser drivers top.u_core.result_o`, `loads ...`: what drives a signal, what it drives (instance paths,
  with generate labels and iterations: `top.g_lane[1].data`; a select keeps its bits: `top.data[5]`).
- `hdl-parser trace <src> <dst>`: how one signal reaches another one, hop by hop. `--through-regs`, `--data-only`.
- `hdl-parser elaborate <top> --path u_a.g[1].u_b`: parameter values and port widths of one instance.
- `hdl-parser evaluate '<expr>' <module>`: value of an expression, i.e. `'$clog2(DEPTH)+1'`.
- `hdl-parser project`: everything as one JSON document. `hdl-parser schema`: its JSON Schema.

Lists are limited to 100 entries (`--limit`, 0 for no limit), the rest is counted in `omitted`.
A list of objects is always a table `{"columns": [...], "rows": [...]}`, even if empty.
Exit codes: 0 answer, 1 internal failure, 2 usage or bad argument, 3 name not found (with suggestions).
Macros are not expanded by default: `--expand-macros` (`-e`), `-D NAME=VALUE`, `-I <dir>`.
`-r` removes `` `ifdef `` branches which are not compiled, `--closed-world` treats macros defined nowhere as
undefined (use it with the complete defines of the filelist; otherwise both branches of such an `` `ifdef `` stay).
Options can be kept in `hdl-parser.toml` (current directory or a parent): `filelist`, `expand_macros`,
`resolve_ifdefs`, `closed_world`, `defines`, `inc_dirs`, `cache_dir`, `blackbox`, ... Then no options are needed.
Elaborated values are never guessed: what cannot be computed has `unknown` with the reason.

## Docs

- [Guide for AI agents](https://hdl-parser.readthedocs.io/en/stable/agents/): one worked example per query
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/ericsmacedo/hdl-parser/blob/main/skills/hdl-parser/SKILL.md): setup, workflow, pitfalls
- [Skill reference](https://github.com/ericsmacedo/hdl-parser/blob/main/skills/hdl-parser/reference.md): every MCP tool argument
- [Usage](https://hdl-parser.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage/): what is extracted, projects, macros
- [Query API](https://hdl-parser.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api-query/): the same queries in Python
- [Data model](https://hdl-parser.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api-datamodel/): all fields
- [JSON Schema](https://hdl-parser.readthedocs.io/en/stable/schema/project.schema.json): format of `hdl-parser project`
